name: Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management
description:
The advanced diploma builds directly on Greenwich's Diploma of Hospitality Management, moving from shift-level operations into venue-level strategy: financial performance across a whole property, workforce planning, and strategic marketing and business planning for a hospitality operation rather than a single department.

Students typically arrive at this qualification either having completed Greenwich's standard hospitality diploma or with several years of unaccredited hospitality supervisory experience they want formally recognised. The strategic-planning units mean assessment shifts from the more operational, task-based work of the standard diploma toward business-planning documents and analysis.

It carries the strongest credit-transfer weighting among Greenwich's hospitality qualifications, letting graduates enter a partner university hospitality or business degree with a substantial head start, or move directly into venue or operations management roles.
curriculum:
Core units: Develop and Implement Business Plans, Manage Physical Assets, Manage Finance Within a Budget, Roster Staff, Manage Operational Plans, Lead and Manage People
Electives: Manage Ethical Business Practices, Manage Business Risk, Develop and Manage Marketing Strategies
Capstone: venue-level business plan or strategic management project
Pathway: credit toward advanced-standing entry into a partner university hospitality or business degree
admission_requirements: Diploma of Hospitality Management or equivalent industry experience

name: Advanced Diploma of Information Technology
description:
This advanced diploma runs deeper than a first-year IT unit, covering network design, systems analysis, database design and project-based development work, and it's positioned specifically for students who want maximum credit transfer into a partner university's IT or computer science degree. Greenwich markets the advanced diploma route as the fastest legitimate way to reach second- or third-year standing in an IT bachelor's.

Because the field moves fast, Greenwich updates elective offerings between intakes to track current employer demand: cloud fundamentals and cybersecurity basics have become more prominent additions to the elective pool in recent years, alongside the more constant core of networking and database work.

Graduates either move directly into junior technical support, network administration or junior developer roles, or continue into a partner university IT degree with substantial advanced standing already banked.
curriculum:
Core units: Design Database Solutions, Design and Implement a Server Infrastructure, Automate Processes for Business Requirements, Design Enterprise Wireless Local Area Networks, Manage Data in the Database
Electives: Manage Network Security, Cloud Computing Fundamentals, Develop Advanced Web Applications
Capstone: applied systems or network design project
Pathway: credit toward second- or third-year entry into a partner university IT or computer science degree

name: Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Management
description:
The advanced diploma sits a level above Greenwich's standard leadership and management diploma and assumes students either already hold that diploma or bring equivalent supervisory experience: the coursework moves quickly into strategic-level tasks (leading organisational change, strategic planning, developing workplace policy) rather than repeating first-line management basics.

Because it's pitched at people already functioning in, or close to, a team-leader role, Greenwich runs a fair amount of the assessment around each student's own workplace or a detailed case organisation, so two students in the same cohort can end up producing quite different portfolios depending on the industry they're aiming at.

The advanced diploma carries the strongest credit weighting of Greenwich's business-adjacent qualifications, and students most often use it to enter directly into the second or third year of a partner university's business or management degree, or to move straight into a team leader or supervisor role without continuing to a bachelor's at all.
curriculum:
Core units: Lead Strategic Planning Processes, Develop Organisational Systems, Lead and Manage Organisational Change, Manage Strategic Financial Resources, Undertake Strategic Workforce Planning
Electives: Manage Innovation and Continuous Improvement, Manage Business Risk, Manage Business Operational Plans
Capstone: workplace-based (or case-organisation) strategic management portfolio
Pathway: credit toward second- or third-year entry into a partner university business or management degree
admission_requirements: Diploma of Leadership and Management or equivalent industry experience

name: Diploma of Business
description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Business is a nationally recognised VET qualification, not a taste of a university degree: the assessment is built around workplace tasks (drafting a business plan, running a budget, writing up a risk register) rather than essays, which suits students who learn better by producing something usable than by writing about theory. Most students enrol specifically because it converts into credit toward a partner university's business degree, shaving up to a year off a bachelor's when the pathway is followed through.

Class sizes at Greenwich's Sydney CBD campus are kept small by design, and a large share of the cohort is international students building English proficiency and local business fluency alongside the qualification itself. Group projects and presentations get more classroom time here than they typically would in a standard first-year university subject, which is deliberate scaffolding rather than a lighter workload.

Graduates either step straight into junior business, admin or coordinator roles or, more commonly, use the diploma's credit points to enter the second year of a partner university's Bachelor of Business.
curriculum:
Core units: Develop and Use Emotional Intelligence, Communicate in the Workplace, Undertake Project Work, Apply Business Risk Management Processes, Plan and Manage Budgets and Financial Plans, Contribute to Organisational Development
Electives: Marketing Principles, Human Resources Fundamentals, Workplace Health and Safety Processes (elective selection varies by intake)
Assessment: workplace-style tasks (business plans, budgets, case studies) rather than exams
Pathway: credit toward second-year entry into a partner university Bachelor of Business on successful completion
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, or Certificate IV in Business

name: Diploma of Community Services (Case Management)
description:
This is the more vocationally distinct qualification in Greenwich's diploma suite. It trains students directly in case management practice: needs assessment, care planning, working within legal and ethical frameworks, and coordinating services across the community sector rather than general business or management skills.

Given the sensitivity of the work, assessment leans heavily on scenario-based tasks and reflective practice, and the coursework spends real time on the legal and ethical obligations of case workers (duty of care, confidentiality, mandatory reporting contexts) rather than treating those as a single compliance module.

Students typically use this diploma either as a direct entry credential into community services, disability support or case-work roles, or as credit toward a partner university degree in social work, human services or community welfare. That latter pathway usually requires the student to complete additional units at the university end given how tightly regulated social work degrees are.
curriculum:
Core units: Undertake Case Management, Facilitate the Empowerment of People Receiving Services, Provide Loss and Grief Support, Work Legally and Ethically, Manage Legal and Ethical Compliance, Analyse Impacts of Sociological Factors, Work with Diverse People
Electives: Support Community Participation and Social Inclusion, Coordinate Complex Case Requirements
Assessment: scenario-based case studies, reflective practice tasks, placement-linked activities
Pathway: credit toward partner university community services, human services or social work degrees (subject to individual university credit assessment)

name: Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care
Diploma of Hospitality Management
description:
Greenwich runs this diploma with a genuine operations focus: rostering, cost control, service standards, compliance with liquor and food safety regulation, rather than treating hospitality as a soft add-on to a general business diploma. Sydney's hospitality and tourism sector gives students easy access to real venues for site visits and guest speakers, which the college leans on more than a college in a smaller city could.

Assessment mixes practical skills demonstration with the more conventional written case-study work found in other diplomas, since supervising a shift and managing a budget aren't skills that can be assessed purely on paper. International students make up a large share of this cohort, and the qualification doubles as an entry credential into the hospitality workforce for students not planning to continue into a degree at all.

On successful completion, students can use the diploma for credit into a partner university hospitality or business degree, or move directly into supervisory hospitality roles: duty manager, front office supervisor, functions coordinator.
curriculum:
Core units: Manage Finances Within a Budget, Roster Staff, Monitor Work Operations, Ensure a Safe Workplace, Manage Conflict, Develop and Implement Marketing Strategies, Coordinate Marketing Activities
Electives: Manage Physical Assets, Plan and Monitor In-House Food and Beverage Service, Coordinate Cost-Effective Services
Practical component: rostering, service and compliance tasks assessed via demonstration and workplace scenarios
Pathway: credit toward partner university hospitality or business degree entry

name: Diploma of Leadership and Management
description:
This sits a level below Greenwich's Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Management and is aimed at students moving into a first management or team-leader role rather than those already operating at a senior level. The units cover the basics of leading a team, managing workplace relationships, and building operational plans rather than organisation-wide strategy.

It's one of Greenwich's more flexible diplomas in terms of who enrols: recent graduates aiming at their first supervisory job sit in the same classes as mid-career professionals from overseas whose existing management experience isn't formally recognised in Australia and who need a local, AQF-recognised credential to have that experience taken seriously by Australian employers.

Successful completion carries credit into a partner university business or management degree, typically at second-year entry, and graduates commonly step into team leader, supervisor or coordinator roles.
curriculum:
Core units: Lead and Manage Effective Workplace Relationships, Lead and Manage Team Effectiveness, Communicate Effectively as a Workplace Leader, Establish Networks, Develop and Use Emotional Intelligence
Electives: Manage Operational Plans, Manage Recruitment and Onboarding, Manage Workplace Information Systems
Assessment: workplace scenarios, leadership portfolio, team-based projects
Pathway: credit toward second-year entry into a partner university business or management degree

name: Diploma of Marketing and Communication
description:
The diploma covers both traditional marketing fundamentals (market research, campaign development, brand positioning) and the digital and social media skills that most entry-level marketing roles now expect on day one. The balance is deliberate, since a purely traditional marketing curriculum would leave graduates behind on the tools most Australian marketing teams actually use.

Assessment is built around producing a genuine campaign or communications plan, usually for a real or realistic small business brief, so the portfolio students leave with has actual work samples in it rather than just a transcript. Greenwich's Sydney CBD location also gives students reasonably direct access to the agency and media scene for guest input and, less formally, networking.

Graduates use the diploma either as a direct entry point into junior marketing, communications or social media coordinator roles, or as credit toward a partner university marketing or communications degree.
curriculum:
Core units: Develop Marketing Communication Plans, Undertake Marketing Activities, Interpret Market Trends and Developments, Develop Digital and Social Media Strategies, Coordinate Marketing Activities
Electives: Manage Marketing Campaigns, Analyse Consumer Behaviour, Write Persuasive Copy
Capstone: full campaign or communications plan produced for a real or realistic business brief
Pathway: credit toward partner university marketing or communications degree entry

name: Diploma of Project Management
description:
This diploma teaches project management as a set of applied tools rather than a body of theory. Students work through a project life cycle end to end (scope, schedule, budget, risk, stakeholder communication, close-out) using templates and documentation styles drawn from real workplace project files rather than textbook case studies.

It's a shorter, more focused qualification than Greenwich's general business diploma, and it attracts a slightly different student: people who already have a rough sense of which industry they want to work in (construction, IT, events, government) and want the credential and the practical toolkit specifically, rather than a broad business grounding. The compact structure also makes it one of the faster diploma options on Greenwich's timetable.

Completion carries credit into partner university business or management degrees, and graduates commonly move into project coordinator or project officer roles as a stepping stone toward full project manager positions later.
curriculum:
Core units: Manage Project Scope, Manage Project Time, Manage Project Cost, Manage Project Quality, Manage Project Human Resources, Manage Project Information and Communication, Manage Project Risk, Manage Project Stakeholder Engagement
Capstone: end-to-end project management plan produced for a simulated or real project brief
Pathway: credit toward partner university business or management degree entry
